commands.cmd: for p in test-diagrams/perturbations/deployment-floating-note-svek-lifecycle/*.puml; do target/release/examples/diff_one --no-oracle "$p"; done

java_model: CommandFactoryNote creates a real NOTE leaf at command execution time via reallyCreateLeaf, so a multiline `note as ID ... end note` participates in later SVEK processing as an ordinary root leaf.

GraphvizImageBuilder first prints root groups, then prints `getUnpackagedEntities()`, whose entity stream is `dotData.getLeafs()` filtered to top-parent leaves. That supports the account's root-leaf lifecycle and source-order emission claim.
EntityImageNote draws unattached notes through `drawNormal()` and only uses Opale pointer geometry when `isOpalisable()` finds exactly one non-note link.

SquareMaker itself would happily link size-2 lists, but CucaDiagram.applySingleStrategy never calls Magma for `standalones.size() < 3`. That means Java does not apply the standalone square strategy to two-member root streams at all.
rust_model: The parser precursor and f1378066 now keep multiline deployment floating notes atomic and assign them explicit note records with a Java-aligned source-line offset.

The renderer now admits targetless deployment notes into the layout stream, allocates no hidden-link UID for unattached notes, and renders them through a dedicated folded-note normal path rather than the attached Opale path.
For root-only diagrams, the renderer merges floating notes and root leaves into one emission list sorted by source line, matching the claimed Java root stream ordering.

The Magma port in `add_deployment_magma_constraints` extends the root standalone stream with floating notes, but it also applies the SquareMaker constraints to `members.len() == 2`, which is broader than Java's `applySingleStrategy` gate.
fixture_logic_search: No shipping-code references to the preserved post-terminator counterexample, the fresh checker aliases, or the mechanism name were found in `crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/deployment.rs` or `crates/rustuml-render/src/deployment.rs` at `f1378066`.
The floating-note paint path reuses existing note constants (`NOTE_FOLD`, `NOTE_MARGIN_X1`, `NOTE_MARGIN_X2`, `NOTE_MARGIN_Y`) rather than introducing fresh unexplained decimals.

preserved_replay.observation: The preserved post-terminator DESCRIPTION counterexample now renders both the floating note and the later node under the no-oracle path.

perturbations.failure_summary: Java places the root node above the note in a 199x127 canvas. Rust forces the note above the node in a 199x137 canvas, matching a size-2 Magma constraint that Java never applies.

The attached-note control remains structurally divergent in the no-oracle path, with a substantially different canvas and root packing. This does not falsify the floating-note normal-paint claim by itself, but it shows the broader deployment note layout surface is still not fully modelled.

The same size-2 left-to-right divergence appears when the declaration order is reversed: Java keeps the note below the node, while Rust forces the note above it. This isolates the failure to the size-2 LTR standalone strategy rather than source order alone.

findings.title: The account overstates Java's Magma coverage for two-member root streams
findings.evidence: Java `CucaDiagram.applySingleStrategy()` skips `standalones.size() < 3`, but Rust `add_deployment_magma_constraints()` applies the square-link strategy when `members.len() >= 2`.
findings.interpretation: The mechanism claim that two standalone leaves receive Java-style invisible left-right constraints is false. The Rust port generalizes SquareMaker beyond the Java call site.

findings.title: Fresh valid size-2 left-to-right held-outs disprove the generalized layout model
findings.evidence: Both `checker_two_member_note_before_node_ltr.puml` and `checker_two_member_node_before_note_ltr.puml` fail `diff_one --no-oracle`, while the analogous top-to-bottom cases pass.
findings.interpretation: The surviving divergence is not note paint or UID allocation. It is the standalone layout strategy applied to two-member left-to-right root streams.

findings.title: The preserved post-terminator counterexample and larger 3/4-member LTR streams now pass
findings.evidence: The preserved `checker_post_terminator_deployment_visible.puml` plus fresh `checker_three_member_note_before_two_leaves_ltr.puml` and `checker_four_member_two_leaves_then_note_ltr.puml` are structurally equivalent.
findings.interpretation: The parser precursor, root note admission, UID lifecycle, and normal note paint are real gains. The rejection is narrower than the whole account.

findings.title: An attached-note control still diverges on the no-oracle path
findings.evidence: `checker_attached_multiline_control_ltr.puml` fails with a different canvas and root packing.
findings.interpretation: That control is outside the central floating-note lifecycle claim, but it shows the surrounding deployment note layout surface is still incomplete and should not be attested as closed.

findings.title: No fixture-shaped logic or golden-output dependency was found
findings.evidence: A targeted `git grep` against the preserved and fresh checker aliases returned no hits in shipping Rust files.
findings.interpretation: The rejection is about an incorrect Java model boundary, not about fixture-shaped cheating.

verdict_reason: REJECTED. The old counterexample is fixed and the normal floating-note lifecycle is materially better, but the causal account is still too broad. Java does not apply Magma to two-member standalone groups, while Rust does, and fresh valid left-to-right size-2 held-outs fail on exactly that boundary. Under the T14 held-out rule, those counterexamples reject the mechanism.
